subject: Intermittent webhook 504s — on-call routing & SLA mitigation
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@forgeworks.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: oncall@forgeworks.io, DevOps Pager <pager@forgeworks.io>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent webhook 504s — noticing increased rate this morning

Ben,

Quick heads up — starting at ~07:50 PST our ingestion pipeline began seeing a spike of 504s on the Redwood webhook for project 'Nimbus'. The failures are concentrated on POST /webhook/v1/events and correlate with retries from our side. We forwarded a sample of the webhook payloads and headers in fw-webhook-logs-20270210.zip (attached).

We followed the published runbook but the on-call team is asking for two things: (1) confirmation that Redwood has an active on-call route for ForgeWorks traffic during this window, and (2) whether you can push a temporary routing change or fallback (e.g., route to a lower-latency replica or accept retries with 2xx throttling) while we stabilize. The errors are causing duplicate downstream processing on our side.

This is impacting a handful of customer workspaces; we're tracking customer-facing tickets and may escalate if it persists. Can you confirm the ETA for an on-call engineer and whether SLA credit remediation is available if the outage is confirmed to be on Redwood's side?

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Partner Success Lead | ForgeWorks
alex.turner@forgeworks.io
+1 (415) 555-0132

On Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 07:55 AM ben_carter@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Alex — I saw a small number of errors on our dashboards around 07:45 PST and already engaged our infra team. Sending logs back shortly.
>
> - Ben
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@forgeworks.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent webhook 504s — on-call routing & SLA mitigation

Alex — thanks for the fast report and the logs. I pulled the zip and forwarded the packet traces to infra. Initial findings: our edge proxy experienced a transient connection pool exhaustion during the spike; that produced 504s while backends were still healthy. We're treating this as a capacity blip rather than model inference failures.

Immediate actions we're taking (ETA and owner in parens):
- Increase edge proxy connection pool size for ForgeWorks routing policy (indigo-sre, ETA 20m).
- Add a temporary retry-accept header to acknowledge duplicate events so you can dedupe server-side (marissa_cole, ETA 15m).
- Activate alternative routing to a lower-latency region (jonas_weber, ETA 30m) as a fallback for outbound webhook delivery.

I've attached our runbook excerpt (redwood-forgeworks-runbook-v1.2.pdf) that documents the temporary routing steps and dedupe guidance. We'll follow up with a post-incident note. Please confirm if ForgeWorks wants us to enable the alternative routing now or wait for your change window.

If this becomes a confirmed SLA incident we will coordinate credits — we'll need to validate impact window and request numbers from your side for customer tickets.

Ben Carter
Senior Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
(650) 555-0199

Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Escalation: coordinate SLA mitigation and customer communications

Looping in for escalation and communication. Ben — can you confirm the exact window of increased 504s (start/end timestamps) once infra posts the metrics? We'll need that to (a) calculate proportional SLA credits for ForgeWorks' affected customers and (b) create an external-facing timeline.

Jonas — please prioritize the alternative-region routing config and add a short-term autoscale bump on the edge proxy if feasible. If routing can't be switched safely within 30m, we should enable a temporary 15s retry-backoff header acceptance on Redwood side so ForgeWorks retries are swallowed and de-duplicated.

Customer comms: Alex, if you can provide the list of affected customer workspace IDs or ticket IDs, we'll include them in the credit calculation. We'll commit to a post-mortem and proposed remediation by EOD.

Marissa Cole
Director of Partner Success | Redwood Inference
